title: 3868. Minimum Cost to Equalize Arrays Using Swaps

examples.explanation: Swap nums2[0] = 20 and nums2[1] = 10. nums2 becomes [10, 20]. This operation is free of charge. nums1 and nums2 are now identical. The cost is 0.

Swap nums1[0] = 10 and nums2[0] = 20. nums1 becomes [20, 10]. nums2 becomes [10, 20]. This operation costs 1. Swap nums2[0] = 10 and nums2[1] = 20. nums2 becomes [20, 10]. This operation is free of charge. nums1 and nums2 are now identical. The cost is 1.
It is impossible to make the two arrays identical. Therefore, the answer is -1.

hints: Since swaps inside the same array are free, positions do not matter; only frequencies matter.
Let cnt1[v] and cnt2[v] be frequencies. If cnt1[v] + cnt2[v] is odd for any v, return -1.
Let diff[v] = abs(cnt1[v] - cnt2[v]). Each cross swap fixes two mismatches, so minimum cost = sum(diff[v]) / 4.
